narrative.overview:
# Stage A cNMF on external RA CD4⁺ T single-cell data — transfer test

**Goal:** test whether the Ota et al. Stage A cNMF flow (`prepare → factorize → consensus`) and
its scripts run unchanged on an *external* dataset — patient CD4⁺ T-cell scRNA-seq — rather than
the Perturb-seq pseudobulk they were built for.

**Verdict:** ✅ the pipeline transferred cleanly. All three cNMF CLI steps ran with the paper's
verbatim hyperparameters (100 iters, seed 14, 2000 HVG, consensus dt=0.4); the only changes were
the execution harness (SLURM array → local loop, `--total-workers 16`) and **K=60 → K=30** as the
plan specified. Programs are biologically coherent for CD4 T-cell states.

## Data flow (as planned)

```
RA_CD4T.rds  (Seurat v5; 13,671 genes × 46,578 CD4⁺ T cells; raw counts layer counts.1; gene symbols)
        │  export_counts.R
        ▼
intersect genes with Perturb-measured list (YC/perturbseq_measured.genes.txt, 10,282 symbols)
        │  → 9,405 shared genes
        ▼
build_h5ad.py  (verbatim 0_filter_cells.py QC: mitopercent>0.3 removal, min_genes/counts=100, min_cells=10)
        │  → 46,578 cells × 9,399 genes  (0 cells dropped — data pre-QC'd; 6 genes <10 cells)
        ▼
cnmf prepare  (K=30, --n-iter 100 --seed 14 --numgenes 2000)   ← RA HVG selection (1,999 overdispersed genes)
        │
cnmf factorize (16 workers, 100 replicate NMFs)
        │
cnmf consensus (--components 30 --local-density-threshold 0.4 --show-clustering)
        │
     ┌──┴───────────────────────────┐
     ▼                               ▼
cell × 30 program usages       30 program identity (gene spectra)
```

## Source data provenance

- **Input:** `Hackthron-Claude/Paper/reproduction/data/RA/RA_CD4T.rds`
  Seurat v5, RNA assay (Assay5), raw counts in layer `counts.1`, gene **symbols**.
  87 donors, 6 batches, `Category ∈ {A1, A2, B, Control}`,
  `Annotation_Level2 ∈ {CD4+_T_cm, CD4+_T_em, CD4+_T_naive, Treg}`, `source=RA`.
- **Gene filter:** `Hackthron-Claude/YC/perturbseq_measured.genes.txt` (10,282 Perturb-seq measured
  gene symbols). Intersection with RA genes = **9,405**.

## Outputs — the two deliverables

`cNMF/RA_CD4T/test1/`

| file | shape | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `test1.usages.k_30.dt_0_4.consensus.txt` | 46,578 × 30 | **cell × 30 program usages** (raw consensus) |
| `test1.usages.k_30.dt_0_4.norm.txt` | 46,578 × 30 | usages normalized to sum-to-1 per cell |
| `test1.gene_spectra_score.k_30.dt_0_4.txt` | 30 × 9,399 | **30 program identity** — z-scored gene loadings |
| `test1.gene_spectra_tpm.k_30.dt_0_4.txt` | 30 × 9,399 | TPM-scale gene loadings |
| `test1.spectra.k_30.dt_0_4.consensus.txt` | 30 × 1,999 | consensus spectra (HVG space) |
| `program_top20_genes.csv` | 30 × 20 | top-20 marker genes per program |
| `test1.clustering.k_30.dt_0_4.png` | — | consensus stability / clustergram |

## Program identity (top genes) — biological sanity check

| Program | Top genes | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| P2 | CCR7, SELL, TXNIP, LDHB | Naïve / central-memory |
| P6 | JUN, JUNB, FOS, DUSP1, NFKBIA | AP-1 immediate-early activation |
| P11 | GATA3, CCR4, CCR8, IL7R | Th2 |
| P13 | FOXP3, IKZF2, TIGIT, RTKN2 | Treg (resting) |
| P17 | GZMK, GZMA, CCL5, EOMES, CXCR3 | Cytotoxic / Th1 (GZMK memory) |
| P18 | RORC, CCR6, KLRB1, IL1R1, MAF | Th17 |
| P20 | PDCD1, TOX, TIGIT, TOX2 | Exhaustion / Tfh-like |
| P22 | FOXP3, CTLA4, TNFRSF9, DUSP4 | Activated Treg |
| P24 | STAT1, GBP1/2/4/5, IRF1 | IFN-γ response |
| P25 | MX1, ISG15, IFI6, OAS1, IFIT1/3 | Type-I IFN response |
| P29 | UTY, DDX3Y, USP9Y, KDM5D | Y-chromosome (male donors) |
| P30 | NKG7, GZMB, GNLY, FGFBP2, KLRD1 | Cytotoxic / NK-like |

## Reproduce

```bash
cd /mnt/scratch/ZY2/Hackathon/tcell_perturbseq/cNMF_RA_analysis
export PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1        # ~/.local shadows the conda env on this box
R=/mnt/scratch/ZY2/.envs/env_r_core/bin/Rscript          # Seurat 5.5 (reads the .rds)
PY=/mnt/scratch/ZY2/.envs/perturbseq-repro/bin/python     # scanpy 1.11 + cnmf

$R  RA_CD4T_external/export_counts.R      # Seurat .rds → mtx + genes + barcodes + metadata (gene ∩)
$PY RA_CD4T_external/build_h5ad.py        # → filtered_data/RA_CD4T.h5ad  (verbatim 0_filter QC)
# Stage A: prepare (K=30) → factorize (16 workers) → combine → consensus (dt=0.4)
bash RA_CD4T_external/run_factorize.sh    # (prepare/consensus commands are logged in this README's flow)
$PY RA_CD4T_external/verify_outputs.py    # dims check + normalized usages + program_top20_genes.csv
```

## Notes / caveats

- **Not Perturb-seq.** This is patient scRNA-seq with no CRISPR guide, so only Stage A (program
  discovery) applies. Stages B–C (regulatory β_x(P), trait burden) need a perturbation `gene`
  column and are not runnable on this data.
- Input is per-cell counts (not pseudobulk); cNMF factorized on 46,578 cells directly.
- Env caveat: `PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1` is required — `~/.local` site-packages shadow the conda envs
  on this machine (breaks pandas import otherwise).
narrative.scope:
# Stage B/C on RA-derived programs — isolated run (Stim48hr **and** Rest)

Feeds the **RA program basis** + the **fixed-basis projection** into the paper's Stage B/C, replacing
the two matrices that normally come from running cNMF on Perturb-seq itself.
Fully isolated: everything is written under `run_root/`; the main pipeline tree is touched only
through **read-only symlinks** (`gencode…`, `shet_10bins.txt`, `LoF/`).

Semantics change from *"Perturb programs → trait"* to **"Perturb regulators → RA programs → trait"**.

## The two substitutions

| pipeline input | normally | here |
|---|---|---|
| `test1.usages.k_30.dt_0_4.consensus.txt` (cell × program) | cNMF on Perturb-seq | `../projection[_rest]/Perturb_cell_x_RA_program.tsv` — $U_{\mathrm{Perturb}\rightarrow\mathrm{RA}}$ |
| `test1.gene_spectra_score.k_30.dt_0_4.txt` (program × gene) | cNMF on Perturb-seq | RA's own `gene_spectra_score`, 30 × 9,399, symbol→ENSG (all map, 1:1) |

`gene_spectra_score` is **not** the projection basis (that was `gene_spectra_tpm`). Stage C uses it
only to rank each program's top-100 genes, which is why its 56% negative entries are harmless.

## Datasets, traits, layout

`K=30`. Two Perturb-seq states, three LoF traits:

| state | CELL | profiles | NTC | estimable programs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stim48hr | `RAprog_GWCD4i_stim48` | 78,280 | 3,441 | 25 |
| Rest | `RAprog_GWCD4i_rest` | 77,087 | 3,387 | 26 |

Traits: `Genebass_RA_custom`, `Genebass_RA_M06`, `Genebass_RF` (rheumatoid factor).

```
stageBC/
  scripts/prepare_inputs_generic.py <stim48|rest>   stage the 2 matrices; decide estimability
  scripts/4_regulatory_effectsize_RAprog.R          Stage B (copy of 4_..._pseudobulk.R)
  scripts/5_burden_RAprog_oneprogram.R              Stage C (copy of 5_..._oneprogram.R)
  scripts/run_stageBC.sh / run_traits.sh / run_rest_all.sh
  scripts/plot_fig4C_RAprog.R  + render_all_figs.sh Fig 4C, both states x 3 traits
  run_root/data/…                                   all inputs + ALL outputs (isolated)
  run_root/program_estimability_{stim48,rest}.tsv   nz_all, nz_ctrl, sd_ctrl, estimable
  RA_program_x_2states_x_3traits_burden.tsv         merged summary (with names + reliability)
  figures_stim48/, figures_rest/                    Fig4C_*.{png,pdf}
```

Stage B (β) is **trait-independent** — run once per state, reused across the three traits.

## Adaptations (no scientific logic changed)

The `lm` formula, covariates, effect-size definition, `cor.test`, the s_het regression, the pseudobulk
`>4 profiles` gate, and the 100k `set.seed()` permutation are unchanged.

1. **K parameterised** (the original hardcodes `k_60` / `K60_program*`).
2. **Estimability guard** — see below.
3. **Stage C merges β over estimable programs only**, emitting `NA` regulator rows
   (`program_dead=TRUE`) for the rest. Program-burden is still computed for all 30.

## Reliability tiers — this decides what you may believe

Stage B fits `lm(scale(usage) ~ GROUP + gem_group + n_genes + mitopercent)` on
{a gene's target profiles} ∪ {all NTC controls}.

**Not estimable (`sd(usage[NTC]) == 0`).** Programs 14/15/29 (Stim48hr) crashed `lm` with
*"contrasts can be applied only to factors with 2 or more levels"*: their usage is non-zero in only
17/6/48 of 78,280 profiles and **exactly zero in every NTC control**, so for ~9,640 of 9,657 genes the
subset is constant → `scale()` = NaN → `na.omit` drops every row. Hence a provable criterion:
`sd_ctrl > 0` ⇒ the subset always varies (controls are always present) ⇒ `lm` never fails *and no gene
is ever dropped*. The second half matters: Stage C inner-joins β across programs by `GENE`, so one
degenerate program with a truncated gene set would silently shrink **every** program's regression.
Verified: all β files have exactly 9,657 rows with identical gene sets (md5 match).

**Borderline (estimable but ≤5 non-zero NTC profiles).** `sd_ctrl > 0` is necessary, not sufficient:
a program non-zero in 2 of 3,441 controls yields a β driven by two profiles.

**Technical.** P28 (myeloid ambient/doublet, LYZ/CD14) and P29 (Y-chromosome) are artefacts, not
biology — see [`../annotation/README.md`](../annotation/README.md). Discard their associations.

| tier | Stim48hr | Rest |
|---|---|---|
| not estimable | 2, 9, 14, 15, 29 | 8, 9, 10, 23 |
| ⚠ borderline (≤5 non-zero NTC) | 3 (1 profile), 6 (2) | 1, 2, 3 (2), 6, 14, 16, 20, 28, 29 |
| technical | 28, 29 | 28, 29 |

**Reliable in BOTH states: 16 / 30** — P4, 5, 7, 11, 12, 13, 17, 18, 19, 21, 22, 24, 25, 26, 27, 30.

Figures ring borderline programs in grey and name them in the caption.

## Results

Per-trait Bonferroni: program-burden 0.05/30 = 1.67e-3; regulator-burden 0.05/n_estimable
(2.0e-3 Stim48hr, 1.92e-3 Rest).

### Program-burden is identical in both states — verified byte-for-byte

`diff` of `programs_enrichment_K30_*` between `RAprog_GWCD4i_stim48` and `RAprog_GWCD4i_rest` is
**empty**. This confirms from the data what the code says: program-burden uses only RA's
`gene_spectra_score` + LoF γ + s_het and **never touches Perturb-seq**. Swapping Stim48hr for Rest can
only change the *regulator* axis. The two states are therefore not independent replicates of the
program-burden result.

### Bonferroni-level hits (both problematic)

| state | trait | program | test | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| both | RA_custom | **P23** — Th17 differentiation, IL-6–STAT3 feedback (SOCS3/BATF) | program-burden, P=1.48e-3 | biologically apt; three caveats below |
| Rest | RA_custom | P3 — actin cytoskeleton | regulator-burden, P=1.03e-3 | ❌ **artefact**: β from **2** non-zero NTC profiles of 3,387 |

**P23** is the Th17 program (`T-helper 17 cell differentiation` FE=12.1, q=2.6e-05) — the canonical
RA-associated CD4 state, so the hit is coherent. Still:
1. it does **not** survive correction across traits (30 × 3 = 90 tests; 0.05/90 = 5.6e-4 < 1.48e-3);
2. it does **not** involve Perturb-seq (program-burden, above); P23's regulator-burden is P = 0.52 —
   nothing. In Rest, P23 is not even estimable;
3. its direction is inconsistent across traits: enriched for RA γ (RA_custom P=0.0015; RA_M06 same
   sign, P=0.23) but **depleted** for RF γ (P=0.020).

### Regulator-burden, nominal p<0.05, restricted to reliable programs

This is where the Perturb-seq data actually enters (borderline + technical programs excluded).

| state | trait | programs |
|---|---|---|
| Stim48hr | RA_custom | P30 cytotoxic/NK-like (P=0.026, β=−0.024) |
| Stim48hr | RA_M06 | P11 Th2 (0.033, +0.022); P19 SOCS2/CISH (0.038, −0.022); P26 proliferation (0.039, −0.022); P20 exhaustion (0.040, +0.022) |
| Stim48hr | RF | P12 Tfh/TCR (0.029, +0.026); P22 activated Treg (0.039, −0.024) |
| Rest | RA_custom | *(none)* |
| Rest | RA_M06 | P12 Tfh/TCR (0.004, +0.030) |
| Rest | RF | P18 Th17 (0.018, −0.028); P26 proliferation (0.037, +0.025); P7 cortical actin (0.041, +0.024) |

Nothing survives Bonferroni. **P12 (Tfh-like / TCR signalling)** is the only program nominally
significant in both states, though for different traits (RF in Stim48hr, RA_M06 in Rest);
**P26 (proliferation)** appears in both but with *opposite* β sign.

> ⚠ **Correction to an earlier version of this file**: it reported P6 (AP-1 immediate-early) as
> Stim48hr/RA_custom's best regulator-burden (P=0.0033). P6 is **borderline** — 2 non-zero NTC
> profiles of 3,441 — and that number should not have been quoted as a result.

### Do the regulators agree between states?

For the 16 programs reliable in both states, the correlation of β across the 9,334 shared knockdown
genes is **weak**: median r = **0.121** (range 0.010–0.406; highest P22 activated Treg r=0.41, then
P27 γδ 0.34, P26 proliferation 0.32). Positive but small. Either regulator→program effects are
genuinely state-dependent (the paper's own thesis), or β is noise-dominated at this power. The burden
signal is far too weak to distinguish these.

### Projection quality, Rest vs Stim48hr

| | Stim48hr | Rest |
|---|---|---|
| rel_error median | 0.720 | **0.587** |
| per-cell R² median | 0.481 | **0.656** |
| dead programs | 2 | 1 |

The RA basis fits **Rest markedly better**, which is what you would expect: it was learned from patient
CD4 T cells, which are predominantly resting. The cost is sparser usage of several programs in Rest
(9 borderline vs 2), so Rest's β are individually more fragile even though its reconstruction is better.

## Overall

Reproduces the K=60 Perturb-native conclusion: RA rare loss-of-function burden is underpowered (no
exome-wide-significant genes) and **no program is convincingly trait-associated** in either state.
The gene universe is 9,399 (not 18,108), so top-100 program genes and the s_het-matched null come from
a smaller pool — not directly comparable to the K=60 numbers. Do **not** pair these β with RA's
original `test1.usages…consensus.txt` (different coordinate system, corr 0.71); use
`../projection/RA_cell_x_RA_program.projected.tsv`.

## Relation to Stage B

Stage B (`4_regulatory_effectsize.R`) does **no** projection. It reads a `…usages…consensus.txt` and
fits, per program × per KD gene, `lm(scale(usage) ~ GROUP + gem_group + n_genes + mitopercent)`;
`lm_es` is β. So `Perturb_cell_x_RA_program.tsv` is exactly the object it consumes.

## Reproduce

```bash
cd .../RA_CD4T_external/stageBC
export PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1
PY=/mnt/scratch/ZY2/.envs/perturbseq-repro/bin/python
$PY ../project_perturb_generic.py rest          # U_{Perturb rest -> RA}
$PY scripts/prepare_inputs_generic.py stim48
$PY scripts/prepare_inputs_generic.py rest
DS=stim48 bash scripts/run_stageBC.sh stageB && DS=stim48 bash scripts/run_traits.sh
bash scripts/run_rest_all.sh                    # Rest: Stage B then Stage C x 3 traits
bash scripts/render_all_figs.sh                 # 6 x Fig 4C
```
narrative.conclusions:
# Fig 5a (regulator model) — biological interpretation

Trait = `Genebass_RA_custom`. Regulator programs are the regsubsets-selected 3 in the multiple
regression gamma_x = a + sum_P w_P beta_{x->P} + lambda*shet. Figures:
`figures/Fig5a_regulatorModel_Genebass_RA_custom_RAprog_GWCD4i_{stim48,rest}.png`.

## Selected programs and regulators

| state | program-burden 5 | regsubsets regulators (w_P, P) |
|---|---|---|
| Stim48hr | P23 Th17, P9 Effector-IL2, P6 AP-1, P26 Proliferation, P24 IFN-γ | P8 IL-2-STAT5 (+0.014, 0.19); P20 Tph/exhaustion (+0.014, 0.20); P30 cytotoxic (−0.021, **0.049**) |
| Rest | same 5 | P18 Th17 (−0.057, **0.00099**); P19 SOCS2/CISH (+0.048, **0.0061**); P25 type-I IFN (−0.019, 0.084) |

## Programs — all are documented RA CD4 axes (high confidence)

- **Th17** (P23/P18): canonical RA-driving CD4 subset.
- **Tph / exhaustion** (P20, PD-1/TOX): PD-1^hi CXCR5^- T peripheral helper cells drive
  autoantibodies via IL-21/CXCL13 in RA synovium — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10106688/
- **Cytotoxic / NK-like** (P30, GZMB/GNLY/GZMK): GZMK+ cytotoxic T cells clonally expanded in RA
  synovium; GzmK activates synovial fibroblasts (IL-6) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-49186-0
- **type-I IFN / IFN-γ** (P25/P24): interferon signature is a recognised autoimmune axis.
- **IL-2-STAT5** (P8): low-dose IL-2 is an RA therapeutic axis.
- **SOCS2/CISH cytokine feedback** (P19): JAK-STAT feedback; JAK inhibitors are RA drugs.

Programs being RA-relevant is expected: they come from RA patient cNMF and program-burden weights
them by RA gamma.

## Regulators — down-regulators contain real genes; up-regulators are generic machinery

Reported / biologically meaningful (mostly down-regulators = knockdown lowers the program):
- **VAV1** (stim P30 down): RA GWAS risk locus, esp anti-CCP-negative RA; TCR-proximal GEF —
  https://www.nature.com/articles/gene201649
- **BHLHE40** (stim P8 down): T-cell-intrinsic autoimmune pathogenicity via GM-CSF/Th17, represses
  IL-10 — https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms4551
- **STAT5B** (recurs as down-reg in P8/P18/P19): IL-2/Treg axis; LOF causes immune dysregulation.
- **LCK** (stim P30), **PTEN** (rest P19), **TSC1** (stim P8): TCR kinase / PI3K brake / mTOR
  quiescence — core T-cell tolerance nodes, not RA-specific.

Red flag — up-regulators dominated by nonspecific cellular machinery:
- mitochondrial complex I (NDUFAF3/NDUFS8/NDUFA8), mito-ribosome (MRPS12, MRPL16/35/42…),
  rRNA methylation (NSUN4, GTPBP10) — Rest P18/P19 up-regulators are almost all MRPL genes.
- chromatin/transcription: SAGA (TADA1/TADA2B/SGF29), KDM1A/LSD1, SWI/SNF (SMARCA5/SMARCE1),
  MED12, MTA2, INO80.
Ranking by |beta| surfaces genes that globally shift cell state (metabolism/translation/proliferation),
not RA-specific regulators — an intrinsic bias of the effect-size ranking.

## Robustness

1. Stim48hr and Rest pick DISJOINT regulator programs (P8/P20/P30 vs P18/P19/P25) — model not
   reproducible across states.
2. w_P mostly P≈0.19–0.2; only Rest P18 (0.001) and P19 (0.006) significant, and 3 tests are
   uncorrected.
3. Full 22-program model R^2 ≈ 0.004–0.012.

Single most defensible finding: in resting CD4, **Th17 (P18) emerges as a significant
regulator-program for RA** (w P=0.001) — the most canonical RA axis, in the parsimonious model.
Otherwise treat the regulator→program→trait edges as hypothesis-generating: programs and a few
down-regulators (VAV1, BHLHE40, STAT5B) are credible, but the metabolic-machinery-dominated
up-regulators + cross-state instability + weak P show RA LoF burden cannot yet pin specific regulators.
